item.title: On the slopes of the Snowy Mountain lives a tribe of upright people, With abundant wealth and energy, in the Kosala land. Born in the…
item.description:
On the slopes of the Snowy Mountain lives a tribe of upright people,
With abundant wealth and energy, in the Kosala land.

Born in the solar clan, the Sakya family,
Leaving that family, I went forth, O king.
I have no longing for sensual pleasures.

Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures, abandoning them is security.
I will go, striving; my mind is joyful.

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.1

item.title: Easy to do is a good deed For one who does good; Hard to do is an evil deed For one who does good. Easy…
item.description:
Easy to do is a good deed
For one who does good;
Hard to do is an evil deed
For one who does good.

Easy to do is an evil deed
For one who does evil;
Hard to do is a good deed
For the noble ones.

From: Udāna 5.8

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, a person, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna. Regarding whatever things there are there…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, a person, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna. Regarding whatever things there are there — form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — he contemplates them as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, a boil, a dart, a misfortune, an affliction, as alien, as decaying, as empty, as not-self. After death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in companionship with the devas of the Pure Abodes. This kind of rebirth, bhikkhus, is not shared with ordinary persons.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.124

item.title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: The daughter of King Koñca, With the chief queen, In Mātavatī, Sumedhā was born. Joyfully striving to practice The Teacher's instruction. Skilled…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

The daughter of King Koñca,
With the chief queen,
In Mātavatī,
Sumedhā was born.
Joyfully striving to practice
The Teacher's instruction.

Skilled in virtue, well taught,
Learned, well trained,
Following the Buddha's teaching,
She went to her parents and said:
'Please, mother and father,
Both of you, listen to me!

'I rejoice in Nibbāna,
Even the existence of devas
Is impermanent.
What value are sensual pleasures?
Empty, with little sweetness,
Their harm is great.

'Sensual pleasures are truly bitter,
Like the venom of a poisonous snake.
Only fools are infatuated
With such sensual pleasures.
Those who enjoy sensual pleasures
For a long time
Suffer the torments of hell,
Afflicted and harmed.

'Those who do evil deeds,
Those with evil minds,
Experience painful suffering
In the realm of misery.
Fools do not restrain
Body, speech, and mind.

'Fools of weak wisdom,
Do not think, do not decide,
Do not stop the origin of suffering
When the time for teaching comes,
Do not care to learn,
Do not realize the noble truths.

'These truths, dear mother,
The supreme Buddha taught.
Most beings
Do not understand those truths.
They delight in renewed existence,
Long to be born in heaven.

'Birth in heaven is not lasting,
Existence is impermanent.
Fools are not afraid,
They are always reborn.

'Falling into the four lower realms,
Being born in heaven or human realm —
Hard it is to be born there.
Those who fall into the lower realms,
Into the realm of hell,
Have no chance to go forth.

'Please, both mother and father,
Let me go forth
In the teaching proclaimed
By the One with Ten Powers,
Living at ease,
Striving to end birth and death.

'Why should I delight in renewed existence
With this sinful body,
Empty, without core?
For the purpose of destroying
The craving for renewed existence,
Please let me go forth.

'Now a Buddha has arisen,
The wrong time is abandoned.
The time has now come.
Throughout my life,
I will not injure the precepts and the holy life.'

From: Therīgāthā 16.1

item.title: Bhikkhus, here the third class of samaṇas and brahmins reflects: 'This first class... did not escape Māra's power. This second class... also did not escape…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, here the third class of samaṇas and brahmins reflects: 'This first class... did not escape Māra's power. This second class... also did not escape Māra's power. Let us make a hiding place near the bait spread by Māra and the world's goods. Having made a hiding place there, without entering, without indulging, we will consume the bait and the world's goods. By not entering, not indulging, we will not become confused; not confused, we will not become heedless; not heedless, we will not be at the will of Māra among that bait and those world's goods.' They make a hiding place near the bait... without entering, without indulging, they consume the bait... not becoming confused... not heedless... not at the will of Māra. But then they hold such wrong views as: 'The world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is finite; the world is infinite; ...' Thus, bhikkhus, this third class of samaṇas and brahmins does not escape Māra's power.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 25 – Nivāpasutta

item.title: Knowing thus, seeing thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, liberated from the taint of existence, liberated from the taint of…
item.description:
Knowing thus, seeing thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, liberated from the taint of existence, liberated from the taint of ignorance. When liberated, the knowledge arises: 'I am liberated.' He understands: 'Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no further existence after this life.'

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāassapurasutta

item.title: - Here, bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person, who does not see the noble ones ... does not train in the teaching of the true persons,…
item.description:
- Here, bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person, who does not see the noble ones ... does not train in the teaching of the true persons, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. Such a person, bhikkhus, is called an unlearned ordinary person, bound by the bonds of form, bound by internal and external bonds, one who does not see this shore, does not see the far shore, bound at birth, bound at death, bound when passing from this world to the next.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.117

item.title: Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thinking: 'May I, as long as I eat and swallow one morsel of food, attend to the…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thinking: 'May I, as long as I eat and swallow one morsel of food, attend to the Blessed One's teaching. I have done much in that way.' Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thinking: 'May I, as long as when I breathe in, I breathe out, or after breathing out, I breathe in, attend to the Blessed One's teaching. I have done much in that way.' Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is called one who dwells heedful, who sharpens mindfulness of death well for the destruction of the taints. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will dwell heedful. We will sharpen mindfulness of death well for the destruction of the taints.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.73

item.title: Elder Nun Dhīrā: Dhīrā, experience The experiences of cessation, The calming of thoughts, True happiness. Incline toward Nibbāna, The security from bondage, the unconditioned.
item.description:
Elder Nun Dhīrā:

Dhīrā, experience
The experiences of cessation,
The calming of thoughts,
True happiness.
Incline toward Nibbāna,
The security from bondage, the unconditioned.

From: Therīgāthā 1.6

item.title: By discussion, bhikkhus, a person can be known as capable or incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, evades the question…
item.description:
By discussion, bhikkhus, a person can be known as capable or incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, evades the question with another question, leads the talk outside the matter, shows anger, hatred, and displeasure — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, does not evade the question with another question, does not lead the talk outside the matter, does not show anger, hatred, and displeasure — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is capable of conversation. By discussion, bhikkhus, a person can be known as capable or incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, reviles, strikes, mocks, and seizes upon faults — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, does not revile, does not strike, does not mock, does not seize upon faults — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is capable of conversation.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.67
